title: A door as a sealed state machine

blocks.text: The page suggests sealed types for state machines: only the valid states exist, and the transitions between them are controlled. `Door` models a door whose state is one of three records of a sealed interface `State`: `Opened()`, `Closed()` and `Locked(String code)`.
Write the four transitions. Each takes the current state and returns the next one:
A code matches when its text is the same.
"Refused" means throw `IllegalStateException`. "Unchanged" means return the state you were given. Switch over the state; `State` is sealed, so no `default` is needed.

cases.says: A closed door opens, closes, locks with a code and unlocks with the same code.
Opening a locked door is refused with IllegalStateException.
Locking an open door is refused with IllegalStateException.
Unlocking with the wrong code leaves the door locked with its own code.
A code typed in as a different String object with the same text unlocks the door.

concepts: Sealed states let a state machine define only its valid states and control every transition between them.
